title: Polynomial smoothed complexity of FLIP for Max-Cut
formal: For every graph, after independent edge-weight perturbations with densities bounded by phi on a bounded interval, is every improving single-vertex-flip path of polynomial expected length in n and phi?
context:
Known polynomial bounds for complete or logarithmic-degree graphs do not cover arbitrary graphs.

sentences: FLIP improves a weighted cut by moving one vertex whenever that move increases the cut value.
The question asks whether every improving path has polynomial expected length after independently perturbing edge weights with bounded densities.
Smoothed analysis allows an adversarial graph while using small randomness in numerical data to prevent persistent worst-case degeneracies.
A universal bound would explain why this simple local-search rule can behave efficiently beyond specially structured graphs.
The saved proposal notes that complete-graph and low-degree results do not cover arbitrary graphs, and the expectation must control every improving path rather than a favorable pivot rule alone.
